entries.name: Hard Club
entries.physical_address: Praça do Infante D. Henrique, Porto
entries.acquisition_path_detail: PORTUGAL-SECOND-PASS-30-40-VENUE-POPULATION-01: proven via research/source-investigations/hard-club-porto-02/ (supersedes hard-club-porto-01's HUMAN_REVIEW; decision READY_FOR_ACTIVATION), CORRECTED by research/source-investigations/hard-club-porto-03/ after a live collector's first real run failed with a zero-length AJAX response: the warm-session AJAX endpoint requires the request header 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' (not 'Referer', as -02's prose incorrectly stated) in addition to the session cookie. ingestion/lisbon-porto/run.mjs's collectHardClubPorto() sends this header; see hard-club-porto-03 for isolated live evidence. The historical month-resolution gap recorded below is now RESOLVED: the warm-session AJAX list fragment supplies day+abbreviated-month for every event, and the event's own canonical URL-path slug carries a trailing '-YYYY' segment that this investigation empirically proved (across 22 real events including 3 real year-boundary cases, plus 5 further real historical 'Happy Neo Year' year boundaries in the archive) genuinely tracks the real occurrence year — a fixed, mechanical, two-input DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination (policy v1.2), never inferred from list order/sequence (the prior -01 investigation's correct refusal to do that is unchanged and still respected). See ingestion/hard-club-porto/discovery.mjs's deriveDateFromSlugYearAndDayMonth() and ingestion/hard-club-porto/observation-adapter.mjs. PRIOR FINDING (retained for history, no longer the blocker): A genuine first-party AJAX endpoint was directly found and fetched live: GET /include/ajax_functions.php?action=load-agenda&start=0&langid=1&passo=15 returns a real HTML fragment of dated event cards (real Sep-Dec 2026 titles observed). However, the fragment's own '.data' field carries only a day-of-month, never a month name — a per-event page's sidebar widget shows day+abbreviated-month for the 3 nearest events only, not the full listing — so this bounded proof could not establish an honest, unambiguous month for every card without risking a wrong-month fabrication. Not implemented tonight on that basis (per this task's 'never fabricate' rule), not because the endpoint itself is inaccessible. PORTO-COVERAGE-02 (2026-08-24) revisited this exact gap per that task's own explicit first priority, fetching the CURRENT site again in depth: the per-event detail page (/PT/evento/{slug}/) exposes NO schema.org/JSON-LD, no <time datetime> element, and no calendar/ICS link — its own visible content is the SAME day+abbreviated-month agenda widget, loaded via the same AJAX fragment (confirmed byte-identical shape). One genuinely NEW observation: the event permalink slug itself carries a trailing year suffix (e.g. '.../evento/johnny-hooker-euro-tour-2026-2026/') that DOES appear to track the real event year — walking the full ~22-event agenda in day-of-month order, the day sequence wraps around (28→01, 31→01 [the day-31 event is titled 'MOONSPELL INVICTA HALLOWEEN', corroborating an Oct 31 wrap], 21→29) exactly in step with the slug suffix flipping from '-2026' to '-2027' once. So the YEAR may be honestly derivable from the slug in sequence — but the MONTH remains fundamentally unresolvable: nothing on the listing or any per-event page states which calendar month a given day-of-month wrap actually lands in (a month could be entirely skipped between two listed events with no signal of that gap), and inferring it from wrap-position/sequence is exactly the 'never infer from sequence/order' prohibition this task itself sets. This -02 investigation resolves the gap not via sequence/wrap-order but via the slug's own explicit year digits, an entirely different, source-stated signal.
